text:
zoe_lin: starting thread for NewportAnalytics enterprise POC. Sales needs a clear committed GPU recommendation + autoscale + brief security wording for the SOW. profile below.

carl_nguyen: traffic profile: steady 35 rps (2.1k/min), predictable diurnal pattern. short bursts up to 420 rps for 90-150s (1-3x/day). avg tokens/request ~380, heavy tail to 1400 for batch jobs.

marta_silva: model choice: M-XL-Compact quantized 8-bit. perf bench safe estimate: 10k tokens/s per A100-equivalent under our runtime for mixed seq. use 9k t/s for planning to include overhead.

joseph_kim: quick calc: steady tokens/s = 35 * 380 = 13_300 -> 13_300/9_000 = 1.48 -> baseline 2 GPUs. bursts peak tokens/s = 420 * 380 = 159_600 -> ~17.7 GPUs.

zoe_lin: Sales wants a conservative committed number to include in SOW and a short autoscale snippet they can paste. what's ops suggest?

carl_nguyen: ops rec: reserved=6 (≈3x steady) pinned across 2 AZs, min_gpus=1 to avoid cold starts, burst credit pool for short spikes, and rapid autoscale to elastically add on-demand GPUs during long surges. rationale: balances predictable billing and p95 SLA.

marta_silva: alternative: reserve=3 + large burst pool + proactive KV preheat for expected surge minutes. cheaper commit but higher p95 variability during multi-minute sustained spikes.

joseph_kim: autoscale snippet (pasteable):
```
autoscale_policy:
  reserved_gpus: 6
  min_gpus: 1
  burst_credit_tokens: 1800
  scale_up_condition: p95_latency_ms > 350 OR queue_depth > 60
  scale_down_condition: p95_latency_ms < 240 for 6m
  preheat_strategy: kv_seed_top25pct (synthetic, see security note)
  az_affinity: spread_across=2
```

zoe_lin: good. Sales also asked whether preheat/KV-seed uses customer data and whether we can support customer-run preheat to avoid sharing any prefixes. need a short security sentence.

marta_silva: one-liner: "KV preheat jobs use anonymized synthetic prefixes by default and, for Dedicated/Private deployments, can be executed inside the customer's VPC so no customer data leaves the network; Redwood-managed preheat processes do not receive customer PII."

carl_nguyen: ops blocker from customer: they want guaranteed <300ms p95 under steady load and behavioural SLAs for bursts. clarify what committed=6 buys them.

joseph_kim: with reserved=6 pinned across 2 AZs + min_gpus=1 and preheat KV warm, we expect steady p95 <220ms and most burst spikes <300-350ms for up to ~90s without autoscale. sustained spikes beyond that require on-demand autoscale and will hit variable latency depending on provisioning. include fallbacks in runbook.

zoe_lin: can someone run a quick cost delta: reserve3 vs reserve6 vs reserve2+burst and post concise lines for sales deck? keep it 2-3 bullets.

marta_silva: I can run sim. will post ballpark numbers by EOD. quick verbal tradeoffs for deck:
- reserve2+burst: lower commit, higher variable spend (+~30-50%), p95 less predictable during multi-minute spikes.
- reserve3: moderate commit, moderate variable spend (+~20-30%), improved p95.
- reserve6: higher commit, predictable billing, lower variable spend (~-10-15%) and best p95 SLA.

infra-bot: infra-bot: preheat template created -> job newport-preheat-5055554321, will be scheduled on commit activation. :white_check_mark:

zoe_lin: action items: (1) marta run cost sim and post numeric delta (2) joseph add the autoscale snippet + AZ note to SOW draft (3) carl confirm customer-run preheat instructions for security. i'll update sales after numbers. :thumbsup:
